model: clearing(t) = max(endogenous floor(t), k(t) x arbitrage_opportunity(t)); floor = max(0, arb - marginal cycling cost)

arbitrage_proxy.rte_source: workers/fetch-s1.js RTE_BOL.h4 — the engine's canonical 4 h beginning-of-life RTE, single-sourced (rule #4). The E0 summary table was published at 0.85 and is pinned there; see rte_sensitivity.

crisis_window.basis: named, not fitted — see the module header

symmetric_availability_premium.definition: DE FCR capacity price / mean(DE aFRR up, DE aFRR down) capacity price, same month

baltic_k.accession_note: Every day in this series is POST-accession for all three Baltic TSOs (MARI 2024-10-10; PICASSO Litgrid 2025-03-05, Elering + AST 2025-04-11). BTD serves no complete day before 2025-10-01, so no pre-accession counterfactual exists in this source.

accession_constraint.verdict: The PICASSO/MARI break in ACTIVATION prices is not measurable from this evidence base — no market in it holds a usable pre-accession activation series. The Baltic accessions are additionally all PAST and all before the first day of our own Baltic series, so the break is already embedded in the Baltic level this calibration measures. NO break parameter is carried into the forward model; applying one would double-count.

afrr_activation_de.regime: wholly post-PICASSO (DE acceded 2022-06-22; the series begins 2022-06-21)
afrr_activation_de.down_note: A negative down-activation price means the provider is PAID to absorb energy. The down direction is valued as the charging cost it avoids (da_charge_price - down_price), not as the price itself — see afrrActivationRevenue().

afrr_activation_baltic.per_direction: NOT SERVED — see known_limitation in the source file. The direction split is transferred from Germany; the level is Baltic.
afrr_activation_baltic.known_limitation: NOT per direction — BTD serves one activation series per country per product with no up/down split, so the per-direction model calibrates its DIRECTION SPLIT on Germany and its LEVEL on these. activation_rate exceeds 1.0 on several mFRR months, which a rate cannot; it is count/(days x 96) and the excess indicates the count pools something the denominator does not. Reported, not corrected, and not used as a rate.

floor_displacement.definition: p10 of the monthly (capacity price / arbitrage opportunity) distribution — the fraction of gross arbitrage value a reserve commitment is observed to forgo
floor_displacement.basis: same statistic as the E0 summary table's published floors (p10), recomputed on this phase's arbitrage window
floor_displacement.finding: No product in either market displaces the full gross arbitrage opportunity. The arc specifies the floor as gross arbitrage net of cycling cost; every measured floor sits below that, because a reserve commitment reserves SoC headroom rather than the whole MW (36.B1 simultaneity).

rte_sensitivity.verdict: The arbitrage LEVEL moves by the RTE delta and every ratio moves by its inverse, so the priced clearing price is invariant to within float noise. The exposure that does NOT cancel is the cycling cost, and that already reads RTE from the engine's own rteCurveFor. Nothing in this calibration depends on the 0.85 the E0 table was published with.

fcr.basis: DE ex-crisis trend — the post-crisis within-regime rate is NOT statistically supported (t below 2) and is descriptive only
fcr.evidence_class: measured across a regime shift — upper bound on decay, adopted because it is the conservative direction

convergence.held_flat_is_not_the_default: projectClearing() requires lambda_per_yr and convergeK() throws without it. Holding a multiple flat remains available — pass 0 — but it has to be a stated choice, because omission would default to the flattering direction.

baltic_direction_split_sensitivity.transferred_input: DE down/up activation price ratio at p50
baltic_direction_split_sensitivity.note: A band, not a parameter. `even` asks what happens if the Baltic market is simply not shaped like Germany's; both splits preserve the measured pooled level, so the band isolates the shape and nothing else.
